h: The Third Meal and Mercy Beyond Human Arousal

p: Now, at the third meal of Shabbos
they did not institute Kiddush over wine.
גַּם הַזְּמִירוֹת שֶׁל הָאֲרִ״י הַקָּדוֹשׁ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
Also the zemiros of the holy Arizal, of blessed memory,
and at the third meal after eating;
and it appears from his wording
that this is how he instituted that they be said.
For at the night meal we say,
"Let us invite her now…" and so on,
and at the morning meal we say,
"And I invite to it now…" and so on;
only in the song of the third meal
there is no expression of invitation,
since it is said after eating,
and an expression of invitation does not apply.
why the holy Arizal instituted it so.
In Pri Etz Chaim it is stated
than the holiness of the first two meals,
and Kiddush is not said at it.
And Pri Etz Chaim writes there,
and at the third meal, of Ze'ir Anpin
that at night we eat from the mouth of the Shechinah,
by day from the mouth of Ze'ir Anpin,
and at the third meal from the mouth of Atika.
And this needs to be understood:
And in the sefer Mishnas Chassidim
he brought only the third meal,
eats from the mouth of Atika.
And the reason he did not bring the morning meal
וְהַיְינוּ דְּשָׁם אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְפָרֵשׁ כֵּן
is that there it is impossible to explain so,
from the mouth of Ze'ir Anpin,
and loftier than the level of Ze'ir Anpin.
It also needs to be understood
this order in Pri Etz Chaim.
But it is stated in the holy Zohar,
I testify about myself…" and so on,
these three meals…" and so on;
one, the meal of the holy King;
and one, the meal of Atika Kadisha,
the most hidden of all hidden," and so on.
which is "the meal of the King,"
and afterward, at the third meal,
in truth the holiness of all the Shabbos meals
namely, in that it is said
just as the offerings are called
in that He said and His will was done;
and in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 7b):
their Father in Heaven, we have learned."
And the order of the holinesses is:
at night, the meal of the Queen,
for immediately at the onset of Shabbos
"those who fear My Name, who keep Shabbos,"
and "the awe of Shabbos is upon even the am ha'aretz,"
and accept the yoke of His kingship;
through this Hashem Yisbarach is, as it were, crowned
which is the crown of kingship.
And then the meal is called
for the sake of Yisrael, who are called "reishis,"
in that He spoke and His will was done.
which is the rest and repose,
as Chazal said in Midrash Tanchuma
just as I rested on it"
this is called the meal of Ze'ir Anpin,
for the image of Yaakov Avinu
is engraved on the Throne of Glory;
and it is in that we fulfill
"and you shall walk in His ways" (Devarim 28:9):
just as I rested on it,"
are from the side of Hashem Yisbarach.
But from the side of Yisrael,
as the Idra mentioned above speaks of,
where he said, "never have I neglected
then the holiness of the meals is reckoned
according to what the Jew eats.
from the mouth of Ze'ir Anpin,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פח, א)
the head of Ze'ir Anpin is filled
from Atika Kadisha…" and so on,
of holy apples…" and so on.
from the mouth of Ze'ir Anpin.
הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (מִשְׁלֵי ב, ו)
is in the manner of what it says (Mishlei 2:6):
from His mouth, knowledge and understanding."
And it is stated (Shemos Rabbah, Ki Sisa 41:3):
"To one whom He loves, 'from His mouth'…;
to what may this be compared?
To a king…" and so on;
but that which is in your mouth…" and so on;
but the morsel that is in your mouth.
He took it and gave it to him from his mouth;
And so is the matter here:
the meal of the Jew by day
at the meal of Atika, as said above
from Atika Kadisha to Ze'ir Anpin,
that is, from the mouth of Ze'ir Anpin:
Da'as is the joining of Chochmah and Binah,
through the crownlet of the yud.
And at night, also from the side of the Jew,
from the mouth of the Shechinah,
since the meal is of Chakal Tapuchin;
and it too is from the dew
that descends from Atika Kadisha to Ze'ir Anpin
which is the aspect of the Shechinah.
the pairing of HaKadosh Baruch Hu and His Shechinah,
"Yaakov and his sons rest on it,"
just as I rested on it";
and just as Hashem Yisbarach too
on Shabbos has repose in His world,
may you find favor before Me
just as you have found favor before Me
that all that He had made
even what appears the opposite of good
only so that from it there will come "very good."
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קפד, א)
As is written in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 184a):
except that which emerges from within evil."
So too a Jew has repose
from all that passed over him
Then the meal that the Jew eats
is from the mouth of Atika,
And the repose that Hashem Yisbarach has
is called the meal of Ze'ir Anpin,
"and you shall walk in His ways,"

p: we say an expression of invitation,
for we invite the holiness of Chakal Tapuchin
since it is then the meal of Chakal Tapuchin.
And likewise in the morning, at the second meal,
when the Jew eats from the mouth of Ze'ir Anpin,
we also say an expression of invitation,
for we invite also the holiness of Atika,
which is higher in level than Ze'ir Anpin,
since it is now the meal of Atika,
and we want there to be help
also from the light of this holiness.
Not so at the third meal,
when the Jew eats the meal
then there is no one to whom an invitation applies.
this is not his meal now;
since one eats from the mouth of Atika,
which is higher than the level of Ze'ir Anpin.
Only after one has eaten the meal
who is of "the children of the palace who yearn,"
"to behold the radiance of Ze'ir Anpin,"
since this is his meal now.
And this is the matter regarding Kiddush:
when one eats from the mouth of the Shechinah,
which is an arousal from below,
from which there is arousal above,
to merit the wine of Torah,
which is from the dew of Atika
that fills the head of Ze'ir Anpin
when one eats from the mouth of Ze'ir Anpin,
Not so at the third meal,
when one eats from the mouth of Atika,
and there there is no connection at all
is the aspect of the first utterance,
where darkness and "tohu vavohu" are mentioned,
which are the deeds of the wicked;
for so it arose in His simple will,
that there should first be darkness
and there there is no place at all
Only in the seven lower attributes,
which were emanated toward the world of action,
And the matter of foreknowledge and free choice
the Rambam, of blessed memory, already wrote,
at the end of chapter 5 of Hilchos Teshuvah (5:5),
that a person has no power
the mind of the Creator, and so on.
And the Raavad, of blessed memory, wrote
that it would have been better to leave the matter
in the simplicity of the simple, and so on.
And in truth, like the words of the Rambam, of blessed memory,
it is also stated in the Zohar Chadash,
and so wrote the Arizal, of blessed memory,
that in one place there is foreknowledge
and there there is no free choice at all,
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת פט, ב)
And about this they said in the Gemara (Shabbos 89b):
like these years, which come in order
from the six days of Creation
they shall be made white as snow";
for there there is no place at all
for so Hashem Yisbarach created from the beginning
of the seven days of Creation
does not cancel free choice for man,
עַל זֶה אָמַר הַכָּתוּב (יְשַׁעְיָה נה, ח)
"For My thoughts are not your thoughts,
nor are your ways My ways,"
as the Rambam, of blessed memory, says.
there is no place for Kiddush over wine,
which is an arousal from below
